nodes.notes: Reads the project's incomplete tasks. Retries 3x; failure exits the error output. Sample tasks (one overdue, one future, one no-due-date) are pinned so you can test the Filter credential-free.

nodes.name: Compute Days Overdue
nodes.notes: Normalises each task and computes whole days past due (-1 when it has no due date).

nodes.name: Keep Overdue Tasks
nodes.notes: Keeps only tasks whose due date is in the past (daysOverdue >= 0). A tidy project yields zero items here, so nothing posts.

nodes.name: Format Overdue Alert
nodes.notes: Builds one alert per overdue task, naming the owner. Runs once per item that passed the Filter.

nodes.name: Post Alert to Discord
nodes.notes: Posts one Discord alert per overdue task via webhook. Retries 3x with backoff.

nodes.name: Capture Failure Context
nodes.notes: Error rail: records why the check failed.

nodes.name: Alert: Check Failed
nodes.notes: Error rail: surfaces a broken check so overdue work doesn't go unwatched.

# Notify Discord when an Asana task passes its due date: Asana

**Pattern:** Notifications & Alerts · **Level:** Beginner · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers real-time-alerts work end to end across Asana and Discord.

It moves through 7 working steps plus a 1-node error rail, in this order:

1. Every 6 Hours
2. Get Incomplete Tasks
3. Compute Days Overdue
4. Keep Overdue Tasks
5. Format Overdue Alert
6. Post Alert to Discord
7. Alert: Check Failed

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing real-time-alerts work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Every 6 Hours → Get Incomplete Tasks → Compute Days Overdue → Keep Overdue Tasks → Format Overdue Alert → Post Alert to Discord → Capture Failure Context → Alert: Check Failed

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Asana and Discord aligned by hand for real-time alerts
- Real-time alerts work where "Get Incomplete Tasks" is still a manual step before Asana
- Real-time alerts work that only reaches Asana on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Asana and Discord in step for real-time alerts, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Asana or Discord call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 8 nodes in this real-time-alerts build
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 8 nodes for real-time alerts before wiring Asana
- 8 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for real-time alerts

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Asana access token; Discord webhook URL.
Colour key: 🟦 entry · 🟫 app I/O · ⬜ logic · 🟩 output · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
This runs on a timer; the Asana read is pinned (one overdue, one future, one no-due-date task) so you can test the Filter with no credential. Sample data is pinned on the trigger, so hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow end to end before attaching a single credential. Right-click → Unpin when you go live.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never bundled in a template. Every node that talks to an external service needs its own connection before the first real run — open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Asana access token**
Asana → My Settings → Apps → Manage Developer Apps → Create Personal Access Token. Paste it into n8n's Asana credential.
_Gotcha:_ The token inherits your Asana permissions — it can only read/write projects your own account can see.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy Webhook URL. Paste it into n8n's Discord Webhook credential.
_Gotcha:_ A webhook URL is bound to one channel. Use a separate webhook/credential per channel you post to.

Set each credential up once; it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happens when the event should fire**
Cause: The workflow is still a draft, or its trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate it. The manual test URL is different from the production URL.

**A node shows a red triangle right after import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials note).

**Completed tasks still alert**
Cause: completed_since=now should exclude them, but a stale opt_fields set can hide the flag.
Fix: Keep `completed` in opt_fields and rely on completed_since=now; the read already asks Asana for only incomplete tasks.

**No alerts even though tasks look overdue**
Cause: Tasks have no due_on, or dates are timezone-shifted.
Fix: daysOverdue is -1 without a due date. Confirm the tasks actually carry due_on.

**Provider returns 429**
Cause: You are hitting the API rate limit.
Fix: The node already retries with backoff; widen the schedule interval or lower the batch size to stay under quota.

Still stuck? The **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there.

## Design decisions

No Loop node: the Discord node executes once per item, so the Filter's output *is* the fan-out. 'Days overdue' is computed once so the Filter and the message agree. The read already asks Asana for only incomplete tasks (completed_since=now), so the Filter only has to judge the date — one responsibility per node. Silence on a clean project is deliberate: an alert channel that only speaks up when something's wrong stays trusted.

## Practice exercises

Already production-shaped — deepen it:

1. Escalate tasks over 3 days overdue by @mentioning a role.
2. Group all overdue tasks into one digest instead of a message each.
3. Alert the assignee directly by mapping Asana users to Discord IDs.

## 🛠 Customize me

Cadence is the 6-hour schedule; project is `ASANA_PROJECT_GID`. The overdue rule is in **Compute Days Overdue** + **Keep Overdue Tasks**. Escalate tasks over 3 days overdue by @mentioning a role, or DM assignees by mapping Asana users to Discord IDs.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Asana: a PAT belonging to a service user with access to the one project.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole real-time-alerts payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
